method.selection_policy: LLM-selected market-relevant items from news_digest.json; preserves source metadata and excludes noise.

framework.Equities: Broad equity/risk sentiment; market-moving mega-cap/AI allowed; low-signal single-stock noise excluded.
framework.Commodities: Physical commodity futures framework; supply disruption/demand strength positive; supply increase/demand weakness negative.
framework.FX: USD-centric basket; non-USD currency strength positive; USD/DXY strength negative.
framework.Rates: Bond-price framework; yields up/selloff/higher-for-longer negative; yields down/bond rally/cooler inflation positive.

Equities.title: Stocks rise as SpaceX makes market debut; oil slides on Gulf peace hopes
Equities.reason: Links a major mega-IPO (SpaceX) with broader risk-on flows and easing geopolitical risk (oil down on Gulf peace hopes). Dominant equities narrative = risk-on driven by high-profile tech/IPO demand and improving geopolitical backdrop, so strongly positive for market sentiment and liquidity.

Equities.title: SpaceX’s Retail-Powered Debut Helps Steady Shaky Markets
Equities.reason: Emphasizes retail participation and stabilising effect of a blockbuster IPO on overall market liquidity and sentiment. Reinforces the market-regime story (IPO-driven risk appetite, potential fresh flows into equities).

Equities.title: Wall Street digests record fundraising haul as AI race intensifies
Equities.summary: SpaceX, Anthropic and Alphabet financings highlight investors’ willingness to absorb a torrent of new issuance
Equities.reason: Broad thematic piece: heavy AI-related fundraising and issuance shows investors still willing to fund AI leaders — positive for sector leadership and market risk appetite, but also signals potential supply pressure.

Equities.title: Space stocks slump as blistering rally cools after SpaceX market debut
Equities.reason: Idiosyncratic rotation: investors reallocating into SpaceX caused pressure on rival space stocks. Negative for that sector's near-term momentum; limited broader market relevance but notable sector-level rebalancing risk.

Equities.title: Anthropic suspends new AI tools over US government security concerns
Equities.reason: Regulatory/security action against a major AI player is a negative signal for AI-sector enthusiasm and could temper investor appetite for AI capex stories; meaningful counter-signal to the fundraising/IPO-driven risk-on narrative.

Equities.title: SpaceX Is Coming Early to Your Index. How Worried Should You Be?
Equities.reason: Discusses index inclusion and potential concentration/rebalancing effects. Mildly negative for passive/indexed flows (short-term disruption) but lower relevance vs. primary IPO/risk-on theme.

Rates.title: Bank of England: Hold stance extended as inflation risks linger – TD Securities
Rates.summary: TD Securities economists expect the Bank of England (BoE) to keep Bank Rate at 3.75% with a 7-2 vote as Greene joins Pill in calling for a hike. They highlight persistent inflation pressures, upside risks from energy and airfare, and softer demand.
Rates.reason: Direct BoE policy signal: expectation of a hold with some voters leaning hawkish and persistent inflation risks supports a higher-for-longer UK rate narrative, negative for bond prices. Relatively high relevance given imminent BoE decision and explicit voting dynamics.

Rates.title: BoE expected to hold rates as economists split on next move – Reuters poll
Rates.summary: A Reuters poll released on Friday found that the Bank of England (BoE) is projected to keep the Bank Rate at 3.75% at the June 18 meeting, based on a survey of 65 economists.
Rates.reason: Survey consensus pointing to a BoE hold reinforces the market view of sticky policy and slower easing, which is modestly negative for gilt prices (yields higher/unchanged). Relevance is medium as it's a broad poll rather than new policy action.

Rates.title: For Warsh as Fed chair, silence may be the point
Rates.summary: Kevin Warsh will hold his first Fed meeting, giving markets the first public look at how he'll communicate as chair of the Federal Reserve.
Rates.reason: Change in Fed leadership and the first meetings under a new chair raise policy uncertainty and focus on communication; markets price potential for continued hawkish bias — negative for US Treasuries. High relevance given significance of Fed communication for rates.

Rates.title: Newly led Fed poses wildcard for rockier US indexes
Rates.reason: Headline indicates Fed leadership change is a material market risk that could keep volatility and prevent a sustained bond rally; moderately negative for rates given uncertainty about policy path.

Rates.title: CLO ETFs Boom on Higher Rates, Private Debt Woes
Rates.reason: Market flow piece linking higher rates to investor demand for CLO ETFs and repricing in credit markets; reinforces higher-for-longer narrative and pressure on fixed income — negative for bond prices. Relevance moderate as it's flow/credit-focused rather than central-bank policy.

Rates.title: Diverging Rate Paths Force Reshuffle in Emerging-Market Bets
Rates.reason: Highlights global impact of differing central bank stances (US vs EM) and consequent portfolio reallocations; supports narrative of persistent US/DM yield strength and EM pressure — negative for global bond markets, meaningful relevance for cross-border flows.

Rates.title: Social Security COLA for 2027 may jump to 4.7%, one estimate finds. This chart shows prices driving the increase
Rates.summary: As inflation climbs, Social Security beneficiaries may see a higher cost-of-living adjustment in 2027. Here's which costs spiked most over the past 12 months.
Rates.reason: Rising CPI-driven COLA estimates signal persistent inflation pressures that feed into higher nominal yields and inflation expectations — negative for bonds. Relevance above average due to direct inflation-to-policy transmission.

Rates.title: Monetary policy decisions
Rates.reason: ECB policy communications and decisions are a primary driver of euro area sovereign yields; recent messaging has leaned toward maintaining restrictive settings, which is negative for bond prices. Included for direct central-bank policy relevance.

FX.title: Forecasting the upcoming week: Fed, BoJ, BoE and RBA decisions take center stage
FX.summary: The US Dollar Index (DXY) lost ground during the week, down 0.27% to trade near the 99.80 level as investors prepared for a heavy central bank calendar the following week.
FX.reason: Central-bank-heavy calendar is a dominant FX driver; a weekly DXY decline signals near-term USD softness vs majors. High relevance because Fed/BoJ/BoE/RBA decisions will drive cross-currency flows and volatility.

FX.title: Japanese Yen holds as traders switch focus to BoJ hike and Warsh’s first Fed meeting
FX.summary: The USD/JPY pair trades near the 160.20 region on Friday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) remains slightly under pressure, while investors prepare for a key central bank week featuring the Bank of Japan's (BoJ) policy decision and Kevin Warsh’s first Federal Reserve
FX.reason: USD/JPY near 160 and imminent BoJ decision make JPY a focal FX risk. Elevated USD/JPY (JPY under pressure) implies USD strength vs JPY — material for FX desks and potential intervention watch; high relevance due to BoJ policy implications.

FX.title: Japanese Yen: Weakness raises intervention concerns – Scotiabank
FX.summary: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report USD/JPY is steady but elevated, with recent gains already surpassing prior intervention-trigger levels. A 25 bps Bank of Japan (BoJ) hike on Tuesday is widely anticipated, and markets price nearly on
FX.reason: Intervention risk is a high-consequence FX event. Elevated USD/JPY and mention of prior intervention triggers point to potential official action that could sharply alter flows — strong USD vs JPY narrative (negative sign) with high relevance.

FX.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish forecasts point to higher terminal rate – Nomura
FX.summary: Nomura’s European Economics team, led by Andrzej Szczepaniak and colleagues, notes that the ECB delivered a 25bp hike to a 2.25% depo rate and unveiled more hawkish forecasts.
FX.reason: ECB hikes and hawkish forecasts are supportive for EUR vs USD. This changes yield differentials and is a meaningful macro driver for FX — EUR strength (positive) with above-normal relevance.

FX.title: China tees up digital payments system to compete with dollar
FX.summary: Beijing’s cross-border currency platform will be backed by central banks of Hong Kong, Thailand, UAE and Saudi Arabia
FX.reason: A coordinated cross-border digital payments initiative backed by multiple central banks is a structural FX story that could erode some dollar dominance over time. High directional impact for USD weakness vs alternatives; high relevance for FX regime shifts.

FX.title: South Korean Won: Authorities step up FX stabilisation push – Societe Generale
FX.summary: Societe Generale highlights that South Korean authorities have launched a multi-pronged FX stabilisation package to address short-term USD funding stress and speculative pressures on the Korean Won.
FX.reason: Authorised FX stabilisation measures are explicit central-bank/official FX intervention and will support the KRW / reduce USD funding stress locally. High relevance because official action materially affects flows and local FX risk premia.

FX.title: US officials' comments on Iran negotiations put mild pressure on US Dollar
FX.summary: United States Vice President JD Vance said on Friday that Iran would not receive cash or released funds simply for signing a potential agreement, pushing back against what he described as false information surrounding a possible deal to reopen the Strait of Ho
FX.reason: Official US comments that temper expectations around an Iran deal have mild, direct FX transmission — they put some downward pressure on USD risk premium (USD softening). Moderate relevance as geopolitics drive dollar flows.

FX.title: Euro supported by hawkish ECB rhetoric as British Pound struggles after weak GDP
FX.summary: EUR/GBP holds firm on Friday, with the Euro (EUR) modestly outperforming the British Pound (GBP) as weak UK Gross Domestic Product (GDP) data reinforced signs of a slowing economy. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 0.8633, up from an intraday low
FX.reason: ECB hawkishness versus weak UK GDP supports EUR vs GBP (and indirectly vs USD). This reinforces a EUR-positive cross-market narrative; relevance elevated given concurrent macro and central-bank signals.

FX.title: British Pound stalls as UK GDP shrinks, diplomacy boosts risk mood
FX.summary: The Pound Sterling (GBP) turns negative against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday after UK data showed the economy contracted in April, while rising prospects of an agreement between the US and Iran improved risk appetite.
FX.reason: Weaker UK GDP combined with improved risk appetite is a clear GBP-negative vs USD. Macro data-driven GBP underperformance is relevant to FX positioning and cross-currency flows.

FX.title: US Dollar: Peace deal talk keeps support intact – ING
FX.summary: ING’s Chris Turner notes that a potential US-Iran peace deal has softened the Dollar, but DXY is still holding firm. He highlights that energy supply losses and inflation risks persist unless Oil flows freely through the Strait of Hormuz.
FX.reason: Mixed signal: peace-talks soften the dollar but energy/inflation risks keep DXY supported. Small positive direction (USD mild weakness) with modest relevance—useful as a nuance to the geopolitical/FX narrative.

FX.title: New Zealand Dollar dips as robust US sentiment, inflation data underpin US Dollar
FX.summary: NZD/USD trades around 0.5830 on Friday at the time of writing, down 0.15% on the day as the US Dollar (USD) maintains a firm tone following a series of strong US economic releases.
FX.reason: US data-supported USD strength is depressing NZD/USD. NZD moves are FX-relevant but smaller-market; moderate relevance tied to USD macro momentum.

FX.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: RSI enters overbought territory as bears defend 1.4000
FX.summary: USD/CAD trades on the front foot on Friday as lower Oil prices weigh on the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) amid cautious optimism that the United States (US) and Iran could reach an agreement that would reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
FX.reason: USD/CAD strength linked to falling oil (CAD weakness) is direct FX transmission but this is a technical/price-forecast piece — capped relevance. Net effect: USD/commodity-CCY dynamics favour USD/CAD upside (negative sign).

Commodities.title: Gold clears $4,200 as optimism on Middle East deal dents inflation woes
Commodities.summary: Gold (XAU/USD) price consolidates above the $4,200 figure on Friday as market participants are optimistic about a potential US-Iran deal, set to be signed next week, according to newswires. Meanwhile, households in the US are becoming more optimistic about the
Commodities.reason: Diplomatic progress on a US‑Iran deal is the dominant theme here — easing geopolitical risk should reduce safe‑haven demand for gold. That bearish impulse outweighs short‑term technical/price strength in the article, so overall negative for gold prices with elevated relevance given the macro risk-tu

Commodities.title: Silver price firms on US Dollar weakness amid easing US-Iran haven demand
Commodities.summary: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $67.50 on Friday at the time of writing, up 0.21% on the day. The white metal maintains a positive bias despite improving market sentiment driven by diplomatic progress between the United States (US) and Iran.
Commodities.reason: Same US‑Iran diplomatic progress reduces haven demand for silver (negative), but USD weakness and industrial demand provide partial offset. Net effect modestly negative with normal relevance for metals.

Commodities.title: WTI Price Forecast: RSI points lower as prices remain below key SMAs
Commodities.summary: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) pares some part of earlier losses on Friday as markets seek confirmation of a possible US-Iran agreement, prompting traders to refrain from placing aggressive bearish bets.
Commodities.reason: Technical/price‑forecast piece indicating downward momentum (RSI below key SMAs). These stories are lower signal for fundamental commodity moves, so small bearish directional score and capped relevance per guidance on technical pieces.

Commodities.title: Higher blending targets drive RIN prices close to record highs
Commodities.summary: Compliance credits for biomass-based diesel and ethanol have doubled in value since the start of this year. The credits, known as renewable identification numbers (RINs), have increased in price, mostly because of higher U.S. biofuel blending targets. The comb
Commodities.reason: Higher US biofuel blending targets pushing RINs toward record highs raises refiners' compliance costs and underpins gasoline/refined product prices and crude feedstock demand — bullish for energy commodity pricing and refinery margin dynamics.

Commodities.title: Despite US Help, Little Oil Has Gone Through Strait of Hormuz
Commodities.reason: Reporting that oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain limited despite escorts points to ongoing physical supply constraints and elevated risk premia for oil — materially supportive for crude prices and highly relevant to energy markets.

Commodities.title: CFTC Considers Blocking CME’s 24/7 Oil Contract Bid
Commodities.reason: Regulatory scrutiny of a proposed 24/7 oil contract could constrain market structure/innovation and liquidity in oil futures. This is a modest negative for market functioning and trading efficiency, with limited direct price impact.

Commodities.title: UK forces board sanctioned Russian shadow fleet oil tanker
Commodities.summary: The U.K.'s Ministry of Defence says the SMYRTOS was in the English Channel and will be held off the south coast during investigations.
Commodities.reason: Enforcement action against a sanctioned tanker (shadow fleet) can reduce illicit crude movements and tighten near‑term supply availability; modestly supportive for oil prices given geopolitical/supply implications.

Crypto.title: Wall Street and crypto are crashing into each other as tokenized treasury markets hit $14.6 billion
Crypto.reason: Large tokenized treasury flows signal meaningful institutional on-chain adoption and new liquidity plumbing that can increase capital flows into crypto markets — a materially positive structural development.

Crypto.title: Tokenization mirrors the $20 trillion ETF boom as blockchain and AI converge, Ondo exec says
Crypto.reason: Executive framing that tokenization could scale like ETFs underscores a broad institutional narrative (productization, custody, distribution) that supports sustained inflows and higher valuations for on-chain assets.

Crypto.title: Perpetual futures could become crypto's next ETF moment
Crypto.reason: Product innovation (perpetuals behaving like ETF-style access) can broaden market participation and liquidity — a positive technical and flow-driven development for crypto markets.

Crypto.title: VanEck bets BNB’s real-world usage can stand out in a crowded crypto ETF market
Crypto.reason: Issuer differentiation in the ETF market (BNB use-case focus) is mildly positive for token-specific demand but is a narrower, idiosyncratic story versus market-wide adoption.

Crypto.title: Bloomberg Analyst: Most Bitcoin ETF Investors Have Stayed Put Despite Outflows
Crypto.reason: Resilience of ETF investor base despite short-term outflows suggests stickier long-term demand and lowers tail-risk from redemptions — supportive for bitcoin price stability.

Crypto.title: Wall Street is moving past crypto pilots and deeper into Ethereum, says Etherealize founder
Crypto.reason: Institutional migration from pilots to production use of Ethereum (smart-contract/utilization demand) is a broad adoption signal likely to support ETH demand and on-chain activity.

Crypto.title: Here's what SpaceX's IPO means for its $1.3 billion bitcoin reserve
Crypto.reason: Corporate bitcoin reserves and potential unlocking/liquidity events tied to IPOs introduce flows and balance-sheet considerations; mildly positive as it validates corporate treasury use of BTC.

Crypto.title: FTX's Sam Bankman-Fried loses appeal of criminal conviction on fraud, conspiracy charges
Crypto.reason: High-profile legal defeat reinforces regulatory and reputational risk narratives for crypto, increasing policy scrutiny and weighing on investor sentiment — a significant negative for the sector.

Crypto.title: Crypto’s next billion-dollar hacker may move at superhuman speed
Crypto.reason: Escalating sophistication of hacks increases operational and custody risk; security incidents can trigger rapid outflows and damage confidence — a material negative for crypto markets.

Crypto.title: Stablecoins Were Meant to Disrupt Finance. Instead, They Became Idle Cash.
Crypto.reason: Critique that stablecoins are sitting idle highlights frictions in real-world payments/DeFi utility; modestly negative for narratives around payments adoption and on-chain velocity.

Crypto.title: Kalshi’s crypto perpetuals spark debate over whether they’re futures or swaps
Crypto.reason: Regulatory classification debates over new perpetual products create legal/market structure uncertainty; modest negative because classification impacts market access and compliance costs.
